# Reply-level monitoring: existing Steam evidence threads

This first phase closes the accessibility-only gap for the Steam discussion links already recorded in the reviewed issue ledger. The existing nightly collector now also scans each thread's comment pages, matches original reply authors to reviewed numeric Steam IDs and a current developer badge, and detects new or edited staff text. It does not discover new threads or collect affiliate channels yet. Support engagement is not a developer commitment or proof of a shipped fix.

## Identity and content
`staff.json` is an explicit source-identity registry, independent of the site's Member/Moderator roles. Each account records its relationship, verification evidence, review date and review deadline. Display names, generic moderator badges and quotations inside player comments cannot qualify an account. Unreviewed developer-badged accounts are reported as identity-review gaps rather than automatically trusted. Never add a creator as Team17 staff merely because they are partnered; future affiliate sources require their own attribution category and verified channels.

Only public Steam pages are read; no login, CAPTCHA bypass or account credentials. Requests observe robots.txt, have strict destination/size/time/page limits, wait between requests, retry transient failures once, and stop on access restrictions or rate limiting. Pagination is parsed as data, never executed as JavaScript. Metadata and comment IDs/counts must reconcile before a thread is marked fully scanned. A changing count or repeated page is incomplete, not unchanged.

The output is `official-feed.json.response_monitor`. Responses retain source publication/edit dates, stable comment IDs, direct links, verified authors, content hashes and detection history. Only the latest available reply per thread receives an eighteen-word opening excerpt; full forum bodies and player reply content are not republished. Quoted passages are excluded from staff-wording comparison. Links connect to the whole original response for editorial review. A thread's existing issue association is not proof that every response addresses every issue linked to it.

## Baseline, coverage and scope
The first complete pass establishes each thread's baseline. Previously dated responses found during setup are not new game activity. Later newly discovered old responses are labeled historical discoveries; new replies and text edits are distinct. Failed checks retain previous evidence and last-complete timestamps. Missing replies are marked not observed, never silently declared deleted. Complete page coverage and unresolved speaker verification are reported separately. Discovery outside the existing thread list and affiliate channels remain explicitly off.

Overview displays Staff responses in tracked discussions, coverage by thread, original response dates, direct response links, newest/oldest sorting and a new/edited-since-monitoring filter. Partial, unavailable or more-than-30-hour-old checks cannot appear as an all-clear. The top source-check label refers specifically to announcements instead of implying every discussion was reviewed.

## Operations and verification
The existing nightly workflow already checks out the tracker branch and invokes nightly.py; the integration uses that entry point and writes only official-feed.json during recurring collection. No new schedule is added. A separate release job runs parser, failure, impersonation, quotation, pagination, edit and baseline regressions; Chromium/WebKit check the integrated UI, account/submission regressions, theme contrast and mobile width. Its production check compares ordinary live URLs to committed files. Test accounts are simulated; no real submissions, votes or email are created.

Reviewed bug statuses, curated summaries and all Supabase account/moderation data remain unchanged. Do not call an overall green Actions status complete source coverage: read response_monitor.state, threads_complete/threads_total and identities_pending. The ChatGPT watch should alert on new/edited reply IDs+hashes, newly incomplete coverage, pending identity review and recovery, suppressing unchanged repeats and historical-baseline noise. Manual editorial review still decides any resulting bug-status change.
